The note provided by the team correctly identifies that for Habermas, "law as medium" consists of formal rules governing the system (state and economy), whereas "law as institution" resides in the lifeworld to give shared norms an institutional form. My previous answer had these two concepts reversed relative to this specific theoretical framework. Therefore, law as medium refers to general normative control over systems, while law as institution anchors those values within communicative practices of citizens.
CONFIDENCE: 95
